summary: Block 2 (audit). (1) AUDIT of supervisor/simplify-angular/FIVE-CYCLE-CORE.md: the answer to the brief's central question is that (N) is sound — it is a pointwise fact about the closed essential supports, proved by approximating each direction with generic directions and passing to the closed support, so (6.6) is never applied at the specific direction and there is no simultaneous-exceptional-set problem — but the advertised elimination of Lemma 6.7 is NOT valid: steps 3 and 4 use the validity fact (V) at positions 1,2,4,5, while the paper proves no-common-label only at positions 0 and 3, by a mechanism that needs the endpoint pair and the five cycle edges at y_n. Exhaustive check: (V) at all six positions + (D)+(N)+(R) is unsatisfiable (confirms their finite lemma, 0 solutions, two independent programs), but (V) only at 0,3 has exactly 8 solutions, e.g. S(0)={0,1}, S(1)={2,4}, S(2)={0,3}, S(3)={1,2}, S(4)={0,3}, S(5)={2,4}. All eight die from (NC-1) alone, so the minimal repair is one extra direction fact, not four. (2) TRANSFER-LEDGER.md consolidates topology's Lemma 7.5 substitution and exposition's palette bridge with explicit compiled/source-read grades. (3) LOCAL-CHECK-QUEUE.json gives the serial local queue with toolchain and mathlib commit read from the actual manifest. (4) NOTES.md corrections: deletion-only is not signature identity; pairwise < 1 versus diam = 1 distinguished. No Lean was built in this block.

verified_results.claim: (N) holds at every direction, both ways, for the closed essential supports; it does not lift the a.e. rule (6.6) to the fixed direction
verified_results.grade: proof written out from the paper's text (paper p.41 l.2135-2137); paper-level, not formalised
verified_results.detail: Take G = conull set of (6.6). For i in S(a) and each n pick a_n in S_i cap G cap RG cap B(a,1/n) (positive measure since a is in the closed essential support). Then w(Ra_n)=i+1 on a subsequence, Ra_n in S_{i+1}, Ra_n -> Ra, S_{i+1} closed. The inverse direction uses (6.6) at R^{-1}a_n, i.e. a_n in RG. One fixed null set, used only to select approximants; each position gets an independent proof, so no simultaneous exceptional sets.

escalation.obstacle: (NC-1): at the accumulation point x of a five-cycle locus, with a = lim h_n/|h_n|, the list S(Ra) has no common label (equivalently, is valid).
escalation.definitions: S(u) = {i in Z/5Z : u is in the closed essential support of state i at x}; state i is the set of directions whose palette is the diagonal D_i = {i,i+2}; the five-cycle locus is the set of centres where the transition graph Gamma_x contains the five-cycle.
escalation.hypotheses_available: (6.6) a.e. transition rule; closedness and finiteness of the essential supports; the endpoint argument already gives no-common-label at a and -a; (D) S(u) cap S(Ru) = empty; (N) neighbour existence, both ways.
escalation.attempted: direct application of the printed endpoint zero-area argument (fails: no partner direction u' with u+u' near a centre, and no centre whose five edges are known); derivation from validity at 0,3 plus (D)+(N) (fails: 8 countermodels); weakening to fewer positions (fails: each position individually necessary).
escalation.expected_useful_output: either a proof that S(Ra) has no common label (then the finite core of FIVE-CYCLE-CORE applies as written and Lemma 6.7 is genuinely dead), or an argument that some accumulation configuration realises S(1) = {2,4} (then Lemma 6.7 is not removable and the replacement must keep it).
